episode_title: Episode 32: The Evolution of Freight Fraud
question: How have freight fraud tactics shifted from phone-based identity theft to AI-assisted schemes in carrier onboarding?
transcript_excerpt: When Eric Garcia first started, fraud was primarily over the phone and could be detected by hearing the person's voice or background noise. Now, bad actors use AI and stolen carrier information available online to impersonate real carriers during booking calls, making fraud much harder to detect. The main change has been the adoption of AI tools by fraudsters to make their schemes more convincing.

episode_title: Episode 32: The Evolution of Freight Fraud
question: What compliance steps should carriers take to maintain good standing with brokerages and avoid onboarding delays?
transcript_excerpt: Carriers should keep their Certificate of Insurance (COI) current and update it with the FMCSA before expiration. They should also report new trucks to the FMCSA immediately, keep all contact information updated including phone numbers and emails, and stay proactive about maintaining accurate records. Keeping everything up to date helps save time on both ends of the onboarding process.

question: What verification methods does Fetch Freight use throughout the shipment lifecycle to protect customers from fraudulent carriers?
transcript_excerpt: Fetch Freight collects truck and trailer plate numbers and shares them with customers so they know exactly which carrier and driver will pick up the load. They also provide real-time tracking and alert customers not to load anyone else claiming to pick up the shipment. If carrier insurance expires or a carrier falls out of good standing, Fetch notifies customers immediately to prevent liability issues.
